end.summary:
Ishita practised drawing triangular and square-number dot pictures.
They represented 1, 3, 6, 10 as rows of increasing length.
They described 5 × 5 as 25 dots and explained growth from 4 × 4 to 5 × 5 as 9 new dots.
They practised finding added dots using a new row, new column, and the shared corner; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised showing sequence growth with dot pictures. Ishita correctly built the triangular pattern to 10 dots and explained that a square grows by adding a row, a column, and counting the shared corner once. They also worked through 9, 11, and 25 new dots in square growth; the final explanation would benefit from one more guided check. At home, draw 3 × 3, 4 × 4, and 5 × 5 squares and mark only the dots added each time.
